svg.title: One attention layer, one KV head: what the baseline caches and what Palu caches instead
svg.text: What Palu changes: the K and V projections become low-rank, and the cache stores the latent
Baseline attention: the unmodified model (per KV head)
decode, per step: scores = q_p . K^T, out = softmax(scores) . V, y = out . W_o
cache per token, per layer, per chip (4 KV heads): 4 x (136 + 136) B = 1088 B
baseline on the n300, batch 32: 68 KB/token model-wide -> max context 4096
W ~ U . VT (rank r) from a whitened SVD; the cache keeps h = x . VT^T
V never comes back: softmax . h_v . U_v^T . W_o = softmax . h_v . W_o'
K must come back: RoPE sits between the projection and q . K^T
How the factors are made (offline, on the CPU, once per model)
SVD of W in the whitened basis
per layer for a target ratio
group; nothing else in the model
Two granularities, two calibrated dumps used throughout the study (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct)
Fig. R1. The model keeps its shapes everywhere except inside the two caches and the attention call; the price of the smaller K cache is a rebuild before every use.
